notes: Skill lifts pass rate from 89% → 100% (+11pp) across 3 evals × 1 run each. Clear but modest — baseline Claude already captures many Math Academy principles.

Biggest discriminators (missed by baseline, caught by skill): interleaved/mixed practice, mastery gating before advancing, spaced retrieval of specific missed items (puzzles/flashcards), explicit desirable-difficulty warnings.

On the 'I keep fizzling out' eval both configs scored 12/12. The diagnosis (passive consumption, illusion of comprehension) is well-known enough that Claude reaches it unaided — skill's value-add is marginal here.
Cost: skill adds ~47s (+49%) and ~16k tokens (+71%) per run vs baseline, driven by reading SKILL.md + references. Worth it for the quality lift on domain-specific plans.
All 12 assertions passed with skill on all 3 evals — possible ceiling effect. Consider adding harder, more discriminating assertions or more edge-case prompts in iteration 2 if running another round.
